tasks.name: Design secure access to AWS resources
selection_rules: Prefer temporary role credentials and least privilege over long-lived access keys.
Evaluate identity, resource, boundary, session, and organization policies together; an explicit deny wins.
Use SCPs as permission guardrails, not as grants of permission.
common_confusions: Treating an SCP as an identity policy that grants access.
Using IAM users where federation or roles provide safer temporary access.
Assuming a resource policy always removes the need for identity permissions.

tasks.name: Design secure workloads and applications

topics.name: Security groups, network ACLs, and private connectivity
WAF, Shield, GuardDuty, and workload protection

selection_rules: Choose stateful security groups for resource-level controls and stateless network ACLs for subnet-level controls.
Keep workloads private when public reachability is not required and use managed private endpoints where appropriate.
Match preventive, detective, and responsive services to the stated threat and operational requirement.
common_confusions: Reversing the stateful behavior of security groups and the stateless behavior of network ACLs.
Using NAT gateways to provide unsolicited inbound internet access.
Confusing WAF application-layer filtering with Shield DDoS protection.

tasks.name: Determine appropriate data security controls

topics.name: Data classification, retention, backup, and replication

selection_rules: Select key ownership, rotation, and policy controls according to compliance and cross-account requirements.
Protect data in transit with TLS and use managed certificate lifecycle where the integration supports it.
Treat encryption, retention, backup, and replication as separate controls selected from the requirements.
common_confusions: Assuming encryption alone provides backup or deletion protection.
Ignoring KMS key policy permissions when IAM permissions appear sufficient.
Confusing multi-AZ availability with cross-Region disaster recovery.

tasks.name: Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures

topics.name: Queues, pub/sub, events, and workflow orchestration

selection_rules: Use queues to buffer work and decouple processing rate; use pub/sub when multiple consumers need independent delivery.
Make compute tiers stateless when horizontal scaling and replacement are required.
Choose orchestration when steps, retries, and state transitions must be coordinated explicitly.
common_confusions: Using a notification topic as a durable work queue for one competing-consumer group.
Scaling a stateful application tier without externalizing session state.
Adding synchronous dependencies where asynchronous tolerance is a stated requirement.

tasks.name: Design highly available and/or fault-tolerant architectures

topics.name: Backup/restore, pilot light, warm standby, and active/active
Routing, failover, health checks, quotas, and observability

selection_rules: Use at least two Availability Zones to tolerate an Availability Zone failure when the service supports it.
Select a disaster recovery pattern by explicit RTO, RPO, cost, and operational constraints.
Remove single points of failure and ensure health checks measure the dependency that determines real availability.
common_confusions: Treating read replicas as automatic high-availability failover in every database service.
Choosing active/active when a less expensive strategy meets the RTO and RPO.
Assuming a backup has a usable recovery time without restore testing and automation.

tasks.name: Determine high-performing and/or scalable storage solutions

topics.name: Object, block, and file storage selection
Storage throughput, IOPS, latency, and scaling

selection_rules: Select object, block, or file semantics before optimizing throughput and latency.
Match EBS volume and file-system performance modes to IOPS, throughput, attachment, and sharing requirements.
Choose online, accelerated, or offline transfer according to volume, network, and deadline constraints.
common_confusions: Selecting storage only by capacity while ignoring access semantics.
Assuming all EC2 instances can share a normal EBS volume concurrently.
Using a data-transfer service that does not satisfy the required direction or storage endpoint.

tasks.name: Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions

topics.name: EC2, Lambda, containers, and managed compute selection

selection_rules: Choose compute from execution duration, runtime control, scaling pattern, startup latency, and operational constraints.
Scale on a metric that tracks demand or backlog rather than an unrelated infrastructure metric.
Move latency-sensitive processing closer to users when the workload and consistency model allow it.
common_confusions: Using average CPU for a queue-driven worker when queue depth represents demand better.
Choosing Lambda for workloads that exceed its execution or runtime constraints.
Confusing container orchestration responsibility across ECS, EKS, and Fargate.

tasks.name: Determine high-performing database solutions

topics.name: Relational, key-value, document, and in-memory database selection
Read scaling, connections, capacity, and caching

selection_rules: Start with access patterns, consistency, transactions, relationships, and scale before choosing an engine.
Use read replicas for read scaling and caching for suitable repeated reads; neither replaces correct write design.
Use connection pooling or managed proxies when bursty clients can exhaust database connections.
common_confusions: Selecting DynamoDB merely because a workload is large without validating key access patterns.
Treating ElastiCache as a durable system of record.
Assuming a read replica accepts the same writes as the primary.

tasks.name: Determine high-performing and/or scalable network architectures

topics.name: Application and Network Load Balancer selection
CloudFront, Global Accelerator, VPN, and Direct Connect
VPC addressing, subnets, routing, and scalable topology

selection_rules: Select Layer 7 routing features or Layer 4 performance/static-IP behavior according to protocol requirements.
Use CloudFront for cacheable content and edge delivery; use Global Accelerator for supported non-cacheable global traffic needing static anycast IPs.
Plan non-overlapping address space and routing boundaries before connecting VPCs and on-premises networks.
common_confusions: Choosing an ALB for protocols or static-IP requirements better served by an NLB.
Treating Direct Connect as encrypted by default.
Ignoring overlapping CIDR ranges in connected networks.

tasks.name: Determine high-performing data ingestion and transformation solutions
selection_rules: Choose streaming or batch ingestion from latency, ordering, volume, and consumer requirements.
Separate durable lake storage, catalog/governance, transformation, and query responsibilities.
Use partitioning and compressed columnar formats to reduce analytical scan volume when appropriate.
common_confusions: Using a delivery stream when custom per-record stream processing is required without accounting for its model.
Assuming CSV is optimal for repeated analytical scans.
Confusing data catalog metadata with the underlying stored data.

tasks.name: Design cost-optimized storage solutions

topics.name: EBS, backup, and archive cost optimization
Hybrid storage and transfer cost optimization

selection_rules: Match storage class and lifecycle transitions to access frequency, retrieval time, retention, and minimum-duration constraints.
Right-size provisioned storage performance independently from stored capacity where the service allows it.
Include retrieval and data-transfer charges rather than comparing storage price alone.
common_confusions: Moving short-lived objects into classes with incompatible minimum storage durations.
Treating the lowest per-GB storage tier as cheapest regardless of retrieval frequency.
Retaining obsolete snapshots without lifecycle or retention controls.

tasks.name: Design cost-optimized compute solutions

topics.name: On-Demand, Spot, Savings Plans, and Reserved Instances
Serverless, container, and instance cost trade-offs

selection_rules: Choose commitment discounts for predictable eligible usage and Spot for interruption-tolerant capacity.
Compare utilization and operational overhead when choosing serverless, containers, or instances.
Stop, schedule, hibernate, or scale non-production capacity when availability requirements permit.
common_confusions: Using Spot Instances for an irreplaceable, interruption-intolerant singleton.
Buying commitments before rightsizing and understanding baseline usage.
Assuming serverless is always least expensive at sustained high utilization.

tasks.name: Design cost-optimized database solutions
selection_rules: Match provisioned, autoscaled, or on-demand capacity to workload predictability and utilization.
Retain only the backups and replicas required by recovery, compliance, and read-scaling needs.
Use caching or connection management when it reduces database load enough to justify its own cost and complexity.
common_confusions: Adding replicas for availability or reads without including their ongoing cost.
Choosing an engine by hourly price while ignoring administration and licensing.
Keeping production retention and availability settings for disposable environments without a requirement.

tasks.name: Design cost-optimized network architectures

topics.name: Data-transfer paths and edge caching cost
Peering, Transit Gateway, VPN, and Direct Connect cost

selection_rules: Trace the actual traffic path and direction, including cross-AZ and cross-Region legs, before comparing cost.
Use an appropriate VPC endpoint when private service traffic and expected volume justify it.
Choose connectivity topology from scale, throughput, availability, operations, and total transfer/attachment costs.
common_confusions: Ignoring NAT processing charges for high-volume AWS service traffic.
Centralizing traffic without accounting for cross-AZ and appliance processing charges.
Assuming VPC peering is transitive.
